lines.text: Pick any prime bigger than three. Square it, add seventeen.
lines.caption: Pick any prime bigger than three. Square it, add seventeen.

lines.text: Divide by twelve, and the remainder is ALWAYS the same!
lines.caption: Divide by twelve, and the remainder is ALWAYS the same!

lines.text: Let p be a prime bigger than three. Divide p squared plus seventeen by twelve.
lines.caption: Let p be a prime bigger than three. Divide p squared plus seventeen by twelve.

lines.text: Take seven. Seven squared is forty-nine dots.
lines.caption: Take seven. Seven squared is forty-nine dots.

lines.text: Remove a corner dot, and slide the bottom row to the side.
lines.caption: Remove a corner dot, and slide the bottom row to the side.

lines.text: Now it's a rectangle: six by eight. The neighbors of seven!
lines.caption: Now it's a rectangle: six by eight. The neighbors of seven!

lines.text: One neighbor is a multiple of six, and the other is even.
lines.caption: One neighbor is a multiple of six, and the other is even.

lines.text: So p squared is a multiple of twelve, plus one.
lines.caption: So p squared is a multiple of twelve, plus one.

lines.text: One plus seventeen is eighteen. The remainder is six!
lines.caption: One plus seventeen is eighteen. The remainder is six!

lines.text: Always six, for every prime bigger than three.
lines.caption: Always six, for every prime bigger than three.

lines.text: Why a multiple of six? The full lesson shows two neat ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why a multiple of six? The full lesson shows two neat ways, plus every trap.
